biography.plain_text: Thomas H. Gosnell was an American publisher who led Lawyers Co-operative Publishing, the Rochester legal publishing business founded by his great-grandfather. A Yale graduate, he became its president in 1960, expanded into tax and business information through the Research Institute of America, and arranged the company's sale to Thomson in 1989.

long_biography.plain_text:
American publisher Thomas Gosnell helped move legal reference production from hot metal to computerised typesetting. His company became an IBM test site, receiving manuscripts over telephone lines from several cities. Moving printing and distribution to Webster freed space at its Rochester headquarters for editorial and administrative work.

At Rochester Institute of Technology, he backed science teaching with a $3 million challenge grant for improved facilities. He also funded eight memorial scholarships and an economics professorship. He served on the university's board for fifteen years, including a term as chairman, while supporting its rowing programme.
